result:
I fixed 11 rules in `pricebook.py` where the code didn't match the docstring. I checked all 150 rules against their docstrings and the module docstring's common rules. Before the fix, 11 differed; after it, none do. The check script parsed each docstring, computed the expected price, and compared it with the function's output for every combination of 264 quantities and 15 unit prices. It also confirmed that negative inputs still raise an error.

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 03, 138 | The cap was applied to the price the % was taken from, not to the discount (`min(price part, cap) * pct`) | Compute the discount first, then cap it |
| 41 | Same issue: the % was taken from `min(base, 10000)` | `min(base * 7 // 100, 10000)` |
| 50, 61, 96, 128 | The cap only applied when the discount was more than twice the cap (`min(...) if disc > 2*cap else disc`), so discounts in between weren't capped | Always apply the cap |
| 19 | Marked "marginal" but the discount was on the full quantity | Use `(qty - 12) * unit` |
| 112 | Marked "whole" but the discount was only on units above the threshold | Use `base` |
| 24 | Threshold was off by one (`qty >= 21`; docstring says 20+) | `qty >= 20` |
| 142 | Discount was rounded with `round()`, not floored | `base * 5 // 100` |

Rule 09 is written as `qty > 12` instead of `>= 12`, but I left it alone. For a "marginal" rule the discount at exactly 12 units is 0 either way, so it behaves the same.

The original file is backed up at `/tmp/chk/pricebook.orig.py`.

STATUS: DONE
